# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_a744010448

Run `run_82f46ddee170` · blinded · 2026-10-31 19:44 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 1 | 1 | 702 | nuc_solidity z=-18.3; nuc_form_factor z=-12.3; nuc_area z=-10.4 |

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Microtubule stabilizers 0.55, Actin disruptors 0.20, Eg5 inhibitors 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.07, Microtubule destabilizers 0.05, DNA damage 0.03
- after step 12: Actin disruptors 0.62, Microtubule stabilizers 0.22, Eg5 inhibitors 0.07, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05, Microtubule destabilizers 0.04

## Conclusion

**Actin disruptors** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e9, e7, e8, e10.

Why: NSC 3/4 actin with high similarity outweighs single microscopist call; replicate resolves split.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Dose-response washout with phalloidin F-actin quantification plus anti-tubulin spindle imaging and phospho-H3 mitotic index, side-by-side with a reference compound of the leading class and one of the runner-up class, to test if primary lesion is actin network loss versus stabilized spindles.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Approve. NSC is 3/4 for Actin disruptors across 3 and 10 uM including the 10 uM replicate (similarities 0.68-0.80), resolving the initial 1-1 split; the lone dissent is the 1 uM well at lower similarity 0.57. The strong tubulin/mitotic signal is why the runner-up Microtubule stabilizers remains credible, but dose sequence (multinucleation at 1 uM before mitotic surge) and atlas neighbours support actin as top. Probability 0.62 is appropriately modest given the single microscopist stabilizer call. Budget is exhausted and no free analysis would change the protocol vote.

## Unblinding

Compound: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID [6436219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6436219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (3/4). The Scientist's own call was **Actin disruptors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The final Actin disruptors call was correct for latrunculin B (PMID 41208085), and it was won by replication and atlas voting rather than morphology alone. The initial 1 uM and 10 uM wells split 1-1, but adding the 3 uM well and 10 uM replicate gave NSC 3/4 for Actin disruptors with similarities 0.68-0.80 versus 0.57 for the lone 1 uM Microtubule stabilizers vote, appropriately moving probability from 0.55 stabilizer to 0.62 actin.

I was misled by the magnitude of the tubulin signal: tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.6 and tub_mean z=+50.0 at 10 uM plus frac_mitotic_like z=+36.8 and a microscopist call of Microtubule stabilizers on only 2 fields made hyperintense rounded mitotics look like stabilized spindles. In retrospect the e2 nuc_solidity z=-18.3 multinucleation at 1 uM before the mitotic surge and the dose-dependent tub_mean increase (rho=+0.95) were secondary to cell rounding and actin loss, not primary microtubule stabilization.

What was right:
- Acquiring the 3 uM bridge well and 10 uM replicate to test dose-consistency and reproducibility of the split NSC vote
- Trusting the replicated NSC 3/4 Actin disruptors vote with high similarities 0.68-0.80 over the single-field microscopist stabilizer call
- Reinterpreting extreme tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast hyperintensity and frac_mitotic_like arrest as secondary rounding from actin loss rather than primary stabilization

What was wrong or missed:
- Initial update to 0.55 Microtubule stabilizers overweighting e3 tubulin hyperintensity and e4 microscopist call against e5 atlas split
- Treating e2 low-dose nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity z=-18.3, nuc_form_factor z=-12.3) as Aurora/Eg5-like rather than early actin multinucleation
- Using dose_response of tub_mean and frac_mitotic_like as stabilizer support without an actin counter-measure like phalloidin

Proposed next experiment: Fixed-cell phalloidin F-actin quantification with anti-tubulin spindle imaging and phospho-H3 mitotic index across a washout dose-response of latrunculin B versus reference actin and microtubule-stabilizer controls to test primary actin loss versus secondary mitotic rounding.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [41208085](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41208085/): Actin depolymerization by Latrunculin B can either suppress or promote root gravitropism, depending on the developmental stages in Arabidopsis. *Plant Signal Behav* (2025) — Latrunculin B acts by depolymerizing actin filaments.
- PMID [15030313](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15030313/): Actin depolymerization-induced tyrosine phosphorylation of cortactin: the role of Fer kinase. *Biochem J* (2004) — Actin depolymerization triggers downstream cytoskeletal signaling such as cortactin tyrosine phosphorylation.
